what_this_is: ONE FIXED CAMERA, frames at increasing sim-frame offsets. The camera pose is identical across the pair by construction, so any changed pixel is the scene.
no_appearance_claim: SwiftShader. W1-30-EVIDENCE §4 admits geometry/composition/determinism and refuses appearance; this is a geometry statement.
READ_THIS_BEFORE_THE_NUMBERS__F10_r13: **This tool's `CONTROL_frame_against_itself` is VOID and I am not offering it.** `HAZARDS §30`: `f10-r12-motion-pixels.mjs:104` computes `diff(imgs[0].img, imgs[0].img)` — the same decoded buffer twice — so its 0 is arithmetic and would read 0 on a corrupted decode, a non-deterministic rasteriser or a camera that moved. **The pair numbers below are sound and the control line above them is decoration.** A real determinism control is two INDEPENDENT renders and encodes of the same sim frame; the r12 critic shot one (md5 identical twice, 0 of 2,073,600 changed) and I did not re-shoot it.
what_f10_r13_claims_from_this: Only that the crowd's motion still reaches the screen on this tree: **1.55% of the frame changes over 24 sim frames and 1.72% over 48**, from one fixed camera. It is NOT `RI-VIS10` C3 (b2-iii), which additionally requires >= 60% of those changed pixels to fall inside the drawn NPCs' own screen-space boxes at >= 3x enrichment — that arm needs bone-projected boxes, it is carried from the r12 critic's session, and this whole-frame count is strictly weaker than it.
and_the_honest_look: I opened `motion-t000.png` and `motion-t048.png` side by side. **I cannot see the breathing.** At 0.67-1.53 degrees of bone rotation per person per second that is the expected answer and it matches the r12 critic's own note that a reader expecting a visible weight-shift will be disappointed by the frames. What the two frames DO show at a glance is the thing this round added: the stooped figure at the right of both, with the back rounded and the head carried forward of the shoulder line.
